- *Deramiocel Biologics License Application (BLA) for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) under FDA review; PDUFA target action date of November 22, 2026*
- *Major BLA amendment added two-year open-label extension (OLE) HOPE-3 data and proposed a refined indication focused on upper limb impairment in patients > 9 years old*
- *Two-year HOPE-3 OLE data presented at the World Muscle Society (WMS) Congress: 76% slower upper limb decline after patients switched from placebo to Deramiocel*
- *HOPE-3 cardiac results received the American Heart Association (AHA) Outstanding Research Award in Pediatric Cardiology*
- *Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities of approximately $199 million as of September 30, 2026*
- *Conference call and webcast today at 4:30 p.m. ET*


SAN DIEGO, Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --[Capricor Therapeutics](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=ik-0OyNpvz5auMlOwl7t7u-OuwE_Qq8wtRJEh97bWni3xI9bbk-6_zRu7fSBaQi2mblEuphLQD81-XBFIdCAHB25NCRlwYp_F86iCHRgmhPqnXnSjGPu8Q59l7j50xRIdjg26sjnbL-U6tkroMBTIpS2bK9F_iBlZn1bpTXJQXfJm52aB--6Kn6N6NGa_UGNSC5xOWmLRTdxJsPb50dWG53wpCjUqSOYZQgDNY22snrYEMY2qgWDyRvewoSv6v1cY5-Fb14bjA0ffhhMmojYMD-IULs3Wxf3R8tN5jB55w8PcIWSoJuzIKBkARYY62y1XsX9OXXGaL3H_NxjiLvoSX_Ag0tG86YEmNHN9paHGQCWyQlRySHtSo4l5AgNQIMZ_TAP3GOgUFbVjRefBbYl1E3hwUFx4AM5JM-BPjDMuXlAQdgC-pHKb3CmoJVEoI39) (NASDAQ: CAPR), a biotechnology company developing transformative cell and exosome-based therapeutics for the treatment of rare diseases, today announced its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a corporate update.


“This quarter, we took important steps forward on both our regulatory filing and our launch readiness, submitting two-year HOPE-3 OLE data in a major amendment to our BLA while advancing our manufacturing and commercial preparations. In the OLE phase, patients who switched from placebo to Deramiocel saw their upper limb decline slow by 76% compared with their year on placebo, and this past weekend our HOPE-3 cardiac results received the AHA Outstanding Research Award in Pediatric Cardiology. As Duchenne progresses, boys and young men lose the use of their arms and hands, and with it their independence, which is what Deramiocel is designed to slow. We appreciate the FDA’s engagement throughout this review and are encouraged by the Agency’s current focus on rare disease, including its recently launched Rare Disease Framework Initiative. As we approach our PDUFA date, we remain confident in the strength of our data. With our San Diego facility operational, we are prepared to move quickly to bring Deramiocel to patients, if approved,” said Linda Marbán, Ph.D., Capricor’s Chief Executive Officer.


**Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights**


- **BLA Under Review; PDUFA November 22:** Capricor continues to work with the FDA on its review of the BLA for Deramiocel, the Company’s investigational cell therapy for DMD. In August, the Company submitted two-year OLE data and additional robustness analyses from HOPE-3, its randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial, and an integrated summary of efficacy across HOPE-2 and HOPE-3. The submission also proposed a refined indication focused on upper limb impairment in patients > 9 years old – the population studied in HOPE-3 and the focus of its primary endpoint. The FDA classified the submission as a major amendment, extending the review by three months to November 22, 2026.
- **FDA Clinical Trial Inspection:** As part of the BLA review, the FDA conducted a Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO) inspection in July 2026 and issued a Form 483 with one observation. The Company has submitted its response and is awaiting FDA feedback.
- **Two-Year HOPE-3 OLE Data Presented at WMS** **:** In October, Capricor presented the two-year HOPE-3 OLE data as a[late-breaking poster](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_a586b470fdde7effdb116c0f6e0c4446/capricor/files/CAPR_%28WMS_2026_Late-breaking_Poster%29_HOPE-3_2-Year_OLE_cross-phase_data.pdf) at the 31st Annual WMS Congress. Patients who switched from placebo to Deramiocel after year one declined 1.56 points less on the Performance of the Upper Limb (PUL 2.0) scale, a validated assessment of arm and hand function, than they had in their year on placebo – a 76% slowing in this open-label, cross-phase comparison. Patients treated with Deramiocel maintained a slower rate of decline over two years, supporting the durability of the treatment effect.
- **HOPE-3 Cardiac Data Win AHA Outstanding Research Award:** On November 7, Jonathan Soslow, M.D., MSCI, of Vanderbilt University Medical Center presented results showing slower progression of myocardial fibrosis (heart muscle scarring) with Deramiocel versus placebo and, in patients with cardiomyopathy, left ventricular ejection fraction favoring Deramiocel. Results were generally consistent when compared with a matched natural history group. Additional details are available in the Company’s[press release](https://www.capricor.com/investors/news-events/press-releases/detail/358/capricors-hope-3-phase-3-cardiac-results-for-deramiocel) issued November 9, 2026.
- **HOPE-3 Results Published in**[The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01385-1/fulltext) **:** The paper, published in July, reported a statistically significant slowing of upper limb disease progression with Deramiocel as measured by PUL 2.0 (p=0.029), with supportive results across additional functional and cardiac measures.
- **Manufacturing and Launch Readiness:** The Company’s GMP facility in San Diego is positioned to support an initial commercial launch, if Deramiocel is approved. A second-floor cleanroom expansion is underway, with validation targeted for the first half of 2027. Launch preparations span distribution, patient support, market access, reimbursement, medical affairs and physician education.
- **Pipeline:** Capricor has initiated regulatory engagement in Europe and Japan for Deramiocel. Expansion into younger DMD patients and Becker muscular dystrophy remains an area of focus, with next steps to be informed by the U.S. regulatory outcome for Deramiocel. Programs not directly related to Deramiocel, including the Company’s exosome-based platform, have been slowed to prioritize Deramiocel pending further regulatory clarity.
- **NS Pharma Dispute:** Capricor continues to pursue its contractual dispute with Nippon Shinyaku and its U.S. subsidiary, NS Pharma, regarding the Deramiocel distribution agreement. As previously disclosed, Capricor withdrew its motion for a preliminary injunction, without prejudice, to resolve the dispute in arbitration following the FDA’s decision. The Company expects the arbitration hearing to commence in mid-2027.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results**


- **Cash Position:** Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities totaled approximately $198.5 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $318.1 million as of December 31, 2025. From January 1, 2026, through November 10, 2026, the Company has not sold any shares under its at-the-market (ATM) program.
- **Revenue:** There was no revenue recognized for the first three quarters of 2026 or 2025.
- **Costs and Expenses:** Total operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were approximately $44.7 million, compared to approximately $26.3 million for the third quarter of 2025. Total operating expenses for the first three quarters of 2026 were approximately $124.4 million, compared to approximately $79.0 million for the first three quarters of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by pre-commercial activities and manufacturing scale-up. Additionally, the Company implemented a workforce reduction in the third quarter affecting approximately 10% of its employees to reduce operating expenses and align resources with its priorities.
- **Net Loss:** The Company reported a net loss of approximately $42.7 million, or $0.73 per share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net loss of approximately $24.6 million, or $0.54 per share, for the third quarter of 2025. The net loss for the first three quarters of 2026 was approximately $117.3 million, or $2.03 per share, compared to a net loss of approximately $74.9 million, or $1.64 per share, for the first three quarters of 2025.
- **Financial Outlook:** The Company believes that, based on its current operating plan and financial resources, its available cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities are sufficient to fund its operating capital requirements for at least the next twelve months. The Company expects to provide additional guidance on its longer-term financial outlook following greater regulatory clarity, which will inform future strategic and capital allocation decisions. This outlook excludes any potential revenue from product sales, the potential monetization of a Priority Review Voucher, if received, and other non-operating sources of capital.

**About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy**


Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe, X-linked genetic disorder characterized by progressive muscle degeneration affecting the skeletal, respiratory, and cardiac muscles. It is caused by the absence of functional dystrophin, a key structural protein in muscle cells. DMD affects approximately 15,000 individuals in the United States, primarily males. Over time, deterioration of the heart muscle leads to cardiomyopathy and heart failure, the leading cause of death in DMD. There is no cure, and treatment options remain limited.


**About Deramiocel**


Deramiocel (CAP-1002) consists of allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cells (CDCs), a rare population of cardiac cells that have been shown in preclinical and clinical studies to exert immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic actions in the preservation of skeletal and cardiac muscle function in muscular dystrophies such as DMD. CDCs act by secreting extracellular vesicles known as exosomes, which target macrophages and alter their expression profile to adopt a healing rather than pro-inflammatory phenotype. For the treatment of DMD, Deramiocel holds Orphan Drug, RMAT and Rare Pediatric Disease designations in the U.S., and Orphan Drug and ATMP designations in Europe. The Rare Pediatric Disease designation may qualify Capricor for a Priority Review Voucher upon approval.


**About Capricor Therapeutics**


Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR) is a biotechnology company dedicated to advancing cell and exosome-based therapeutics for the treatment of rare diseases. Our lead product candidate, Deramiocel, is an allogeneic cardiac-derived cell therapy in late-stage development for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, evaluated in clinical studies for its potential to preserve skeletal and cardiac muscle function. Capricor is also advancing its proprietary StealthX™ exosome platform for the targeted delivery of oligonucleotides, proteins, and small-molecule therapeutics across a range of diseases. At Capricor, we are committed to delivering new therapies for patients with rare diseases.
